summary: For F/ℚ_p finite and any generalised reductive O-group scheme G (smooth affine, reductive neutral component, finite component group; no condition on p), the framed deformation ring R^□_ρ̄ of a continuous ρ̄ : Γ_F → G(k) is a local complete intersection, O-flat of relative dimension dim G_k([F:ℚ_p] + 1), reduced with normal generic fibre (Theorem 1.1); R^□_ψ → R^□_ρ̄ is flat for ψ the projection to G/G′, and a bijection on irreducible components when π_1(G′) is étale (Theorem 1.2, the Böckle–Juschka conjecture), the components being complete-intersection normal domains, factorial for [F:ℚ_p] ≥ 3 (Theorem 1.3, Corollary 1.4); the same holds with 'fixed partial determinant', covering L-groups and C-groups (§16), and R^ps_G for V. Lafforgue's G-pseudocharacters is equidimensional of the expected dimension (Theorem 1.5). The method generalises Böckle–Iyengar–Paškūnas (the GL_d case): a G-valued space of generic matrices X^gen_{G,ρ̄^ss} defined via condensed continuity, its GIT quotient finite and universally homeomorphic onto Spec R^ps_G, and an induction on dim G bounding special fibres through G-complete reducibility, bounds on reductive subgroups (codimension ≥ 2) and W-special loci. The Böckle–Iyengar–Paškūnas extraction proposed a Part II of LocalGaloisDeformationRings for exactly this theory and asked that this paper extend it, so the route coalesces with it; general inputs go as sources to LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1, DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra, IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants (G-pseudocharacters), ArithmeticGaloisDuality D7 and the condensed foundations layer VS2. One error (Proposition 11.5 is false in characteristic 0, harmlessly for the paper) and one misprint are recorded.

items.name: Theorem 1.1: framed deformation rings are complete intersections of expected dimension
items.statement: Let F/ℚ_p be finite, O the integers of a finite L/ℚ_p with residue field k, G a generalised reductive O-group scheme and ρ̄ : Γ_F → G(k) continuous. Then R^□_ρ̄ is a local complete intersection, flat over O, of relative dimension dim G_k([F:ℚ_p] + 1); in particular every ρ̄ lifts to characteristic zero. Moreover R^□_ρ̄ is reduced and R^□_ρ̄[1/p] is normal.
items.note: The G-valued generalisation of BIP23 Theorem 1.1. BIP23 = Böckle–Iyengar–Paškūnas, On local Galois deformation rings, Forum Math. Pi 11 (2023) e30 (PAPER-BOCKLE-IYENGAR-PASKUNAS-23), the GL_d case. Mazur's presentation O⟦x_1..x_r⟧/(f_1..f_s) with r − s = dim G_k([F:ℚ_p] + 1) plus the bound dim R^□_ρ̄/ϖ ≤ dim G_k([F:ℚ_p] + 1); by Galatius–Venkatesh [29, Lemma 7.5] the derived deformation ring is then homotopy discrete.

items.name: Theorem 1.2: flatness over the abelianisation and components
items.statement: Assume G^0 split over O, G/G^0 constant, ρ̄ : Γ_F → (G/G^0)(k) surjective with kernel Γ_E, μ_{p^∞}(E) ⊂ O. Let G′ be the derived group of G^0, φ : G → G/G′ and ψ = φ∘ρ̄. Then R^□_ψ → R^□_ρ̄ is flat, and if π_1(G′) = ker(G′_sc → G′) is étale it induces a bijection between the sets of irreducible components. Components of R^□_ψ are labelled by characters χ of μ = (μ_{p^∞}(E) ⊗ M)^{Gal(E/F)}, M = X^*(G^0/G′) ([PQ25]).
items.note: The Böckle–Juschka conjecture, proved for GL_d in BIP23; here for generalised reductive G.

items.name: Theorem 1.3 and Corollary 1.4: components are normal complete-intersection domains, factorial for [F:ℚ_p] ≥ 3
items.statement: If π_1(G′) is étale, the component rings R^{□,χ}_ρ̄ and R^{□,χ}_ρ̄/ϖ are complete intersection normal domains, regular in codimension [F:ℚ_p] (in codimension 2[F:ℚ_p] − 1 if no ρ̄^{ss}-compatible R-Levi of codimension 2 exists, e.g. if G/Z(G^0) has no PGL_2 factor). If moreover [F:ℚ_p] ≥ 3 (or [F:ℚ_p] = 2 without such a Levi), they are factorial.
items.note: Factoriality by Grothendieck's parafactoriality theorem ([14], Call–Lyubeznik); for F = ℚ_p BIP23 Remark 4.24 and Corollary 4.25 give counterexamples.

items.name: Deformation problems with fixed partial determinant
items.statement: With G^0 split, G/G^0 = Δ = Gal(E/F) constant and ρ̄^{ss} surjecting onto Δ: a Δ-invariant decomposition M = X^*(G^0/G′) = M_1 ⊕ M_2 gives quotients H_1 = (G/G′)/K_2 and H_2 = (G/G′)/K_1 (K_i = Spec O[M_i]); for a lift ψ_1 : Γ_F → H_1(O) of φ_1∘ρ̄, D^{□,ψ_1}_ρ̄(A) = {ρ_A ∈ D^□_ρ̄(A) : φ_1∘ρ_A = ψ_1 ⊗ A}, pro-represented by R^{□,ψ_1}_ρ̄. M_1 = 0 gives R^□; M_1 = M gives fixed determinant. Z_i ⊂ Z(G^0) are the Δ-stable subtori with Z_i → H_i isogenies (from the central isogeny Z(G^0)^0 → G/G′).
items.note: Generalises the fixed-determinant rings of BIP23 §5; C-groups (§16) are the motivating example.

items.name: Theorems 1.5 and 1.6: the pseudodeformation ring R^ps_G
items.statement: R^ps_G and R^ps_G/ϖ are equidimensional of dimensions d + 1 and d, where d = dim G_k[F:ℚ_p] + dim Z(G)_k (Corollary 13.31). The non-special absolutely irreducible locus U^{n-spcl} ⊂ Spec R^ps_G ∖ {closed point} — geometric points whose attached ρ_x is G-irreducible with H⁰(Γ_F, (Lie G′_sc)^*_x(1)) = 0 — is Zariski dense in Spec R^ps_G, and its special fibre in Spec R^ps_G/ϖ (Corollary 13.32).
items.note: Generalises Böckle–Juschka's theorem [7, Theorem 5.5.1] for GL_d, with a new proof that never uses [7, §5].

items.name: Corollaries 15.23–15.27: reducedness, normality and components of X^gen, X^git and X^ps
items.statement: X^gen_{G,ρ̄^ss} is reduced and X^gen[1/p] is normal; X^git_{G,ρ̄^ss} is reduced, O-flat with normal generic fibre, and X^gen → X^git is a bijection on irreducible components; (X^ps_G[1/p])_red is normal; if π_1(G′) is étale, X^gen → X^gen_{G/G′,ψ^ss} and X^gen → X^git → X^ps_G → X^ps_{G/G′} induce bijections on irreducible components.
items.note: Normality of R^git[1/p] via Bruns–Herzog [12, Prop. 6.4.1].

items.name: Generalised reductive group schemes
items.statement: Over a scheme S, a smooth affine S-group scheme G whose geometric fibres of G^0 are reductive and with G/G^0 → S finite. Over O, G/G^0 is finite étale (Conrad [19, Prop. 3.1.3]); by Cotner [21] (using Alper) G is generalised reductive iff it is geometrically reductive [1, Def. 9.1.1]. Over a perfect field an affine group of finite type that is reduced is smooth, and generalised reductive if its unipotent radical is trivial (Lemma 2.7).
items.note: Tau Ceti's ReductiveGroups plans connected reductive groups and, as a long-horizon item, relative theory over a base (Layer 8); nothing plans non-connected generalised reductive group schemes. The FKP22 extraction's G (smooth over ℤ_p, split reductive G^0, π_0 of order prime to p) is a special case.

items.name: Group-scheme generalities: centres, extensions, fibre dimensions (Lemmas 2.1–2.4)
items.statement: For G flat affine of finite presentation over O: the centre functor Z(G) is a closed subgroup scheme ([SGA3 VIII 6.4]) compatible with base change; in a short exact sequence of affine finitely presented O-groups with flat outer terms, G_2 → G_3 is faithfully flat; dim G_k = dim G_L. Quotients G/N by flat closed normal N are representable (Anantharaman), affine for generalised reductive G, N (Alper).
items.note: Stated from SGA3 and the cited sources; the foundation layer of the Part II imports them.

items.name: Propositions 2.8–2.9 and Lemmas 2.10–2.11: splitting, centres and the derived group
items.statement: For generalised reductive G over O: after a finite unramified L′/L, G/G^0 is constant, G(O′) → (G/G^0)(O′) is surjective and G^0 is split; Z(G) ∩ G^0 is O-flat and dim Z(G)_k = dim Z(G)_L; G → G/G′ is smooth; G acts on Lie(G′_sc) (G′_sc → G′ the simply connected central cover) compatibly with Lie G′_sc → Lie G′.
items.note: Conrad [19] Theorem 3.3.4, 5.3.1, Exercise 6.5.2.

items.name: R-parabolic and R-Levi subgroup schemes (Richardson)
items.statement: For a cocharacter λ : 𝔾_{m,A} → G_A, P_λ (resp. U_λ) represents the points g with lim_{t→0} λ(t)gλ(t)^{−1} existing (resp. equal to 1), L_λ = P_λ ∩ P_{−λ}; subgroups of this form are R-parabolic and R-Levi. L_λ is the centraliser of λ, U_λ ⊲ P_λ, L_λ ⋉ U_λ ≅ P_λ, all smooth (CGP [20]); P ∩ G^0 = P^0 is a parabolic of G^0 with Levi L ∩ G^0, L is generalised reductive, and only finitely many R-parabolics Q have Q^0 = P^0 (Lemma 2.13); for connected reductive G over affine S these are the parabolics (Remark 2.15).
items.note: Tau Ceti's ReductiveGroups Layer 7 names the dynamic approach to parabolics as a parallel route for connected groups; the non-connected version over O is not planned. Example 2.14: in (𝔾_m × 𝔾_m) ⋊ ℤ/2, P_λ = G^0 and P_μ = G have the same neutral component.

items.name: Proposition 2.16: dim L + dim Z(L) ≤ dim G + dim Z(G) − dim U
items.statement: Let G be generalised reductive over a field, L an R-Levi of an R-parabolic P with unipotent radical U, and L/L^0 → G/G^0 an isomorphism. Then dim L + dim Z(L) ≤ dim G + dim Z(G) − dim U.

items.name: Lemmas 2.17–2.19: R-parabolics containing a split maximal torus
items.statement: For G split with G/G^0 constant and T a maximal split torus over O: base change gives bijections between R-parabolics of G, G_s and G_s̄ containing T; there are finitely many, each with a unique R-Levi containing T; every R-parabolic/R-Levi pair of G_x̄ is G^0(κ(x̄))-conjugate to one defined over O and containing T.

items.name: G-semisimplification and G-complete reducibility
items.statement: For G generalised reductive over an algebraically closed κ and ρ : Γ → G(κ): with P a minimal R-parabolic containing ρ(Γ), L an R-Levi, c_{P,L} : P(κ) → (P/U)(κ) ≅ L(κ) ↪ G(κ), the G^0(κ)-class of c_{P,L}∘ρ is independent of choices (Proposition 2.20); this is ρ^{ss} (Definition 2.21). H ⊂ G(κ) is G-completely reducible if every R-parabolic containing H has an R-Levi containing H (Serre; Definition 2.22), and ρ is G-cr iff ρ^{ss} is the class of ρ (Proposition 2.23). H is G-irreducible if it lies in no proper R-parabolic (Definition 2.26); if H ⊂ L ∩ M is L- and M-irreducible then L = gMg^{−1} with g ∈ Z_G(H)^0(κ) (Proposition 2.27).
items.note: After Serre, Complete reducibility (Sém. Bourbaki 2003/04), Bate–Martin–Röhrle and [50, Prop. 2.15]. The atlas plans complete reducibility of parameters only in the Fargues–Scholze setting (LanglandsParameterStacks LP2); G-complete reducibility of subgroups is not planned.

items.name: Proposition 2.24: determinant laws do not see G-semisimplification
items.statement: For ρ : Γ → G(κ) and a closed immersion τ : G ↪ GL_d, the determinant laws of (τ∘ρ)^lin and (τ∘ρ^{ss})^lin agree; hence (τ∘ρ^{ss})^{ss} = (τ∘ρ)^{ss} although (τ∘ρ)^{ss} ≇ τ∘ρ^{ss} in general (Remark 2.25, via Chenevier [15, Theorem 2.12]).
items.note: Proof: the limit lim_{t→0} λ(t)ρλ(t)^{−1} in a constant family of determinants.

items.name: Lemma 2.29: rigidified extensions and generalised 2-cocycles
items.statement: A generalised 2-cocycle of Δ in N is (ω, c), ω : Δ → Aut(N), c : Δ × Δ → N with ω(δ_1)ω(δ_2) = Int(c(δ_1, δ_2))ω(δ_1δ_2), ω(1) = id, c(δ_1, δ_2)c(δ_1δ_2, δ_3) = ω(δ_1)(c(δ_2, δ_3))c(δ_1, δ_2δ_3), c(δ, 1) = c(1, δ) = 1 (Definition 2.28). Rigidified extensions of Δ by N (group laws on N × Δ making N → N × Δ → Δ homomorphisms) correspond bijectively to generalised 2-cocycles.
items.note: Schreier [54], Eilenberg–Mac Lane [24], Zhang [65]. Mathlib has group extensions but not the non-abelian cocycle classification.

items.name: Proposition 2.30: a cover with étale fundamental group and the same κ-points
items.statement: Let G be generalised reductive over a perfect field κ of characteristic p with G^0 split semisimple, G/G^0 = Δ constant and G(κ) ↠ Δ. There is a surjection H → G of generalised reductive groups with kernel μ such that H/H^0 ≅ G/G^0, 0 → μ → H^0 → G^0 → 0 is central with μ(κ) = 1, and π_1(H^0) is étale; moreover H(κ) ≅ G(κ).
items.note: H^0 = (G^0)_sc/K_0 with K_0 the prime-to-p part of the kernel; the component group is re-glued with Lemma 2.29. E.g. PGL_d is replaced by SL_d/μ_m (d = p^e m).

items.name: Coefficient rings Λ and G-valued framed deformation functors D^□_{ρ,G}
items.statement: For κ a finite or local O-field (finite extension of k or of L, or a local field of characteristic p containing k): Λ = O_{L′} (unramified with residue field κ), resp. Λ = κ, resp. Λ = p-adic completion of O_{L′}⟦t⟧[1/t]; 𝔄_Λ the local Artinian Λ-algebras with residue field κ with their natural topologies; D^□_{ρ,G}(A) = continuous ρ_A : Γ → G(A) reducing to ρ, for G smooth affine over O and Γ with Mazur's p-finiteness.
items.note: BIP23 §3.5 for GL_d (routed by that extraction as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1); the G-valued functor belongs there too.

items.name: Lemmas 3.1–3.5: cocycle count, representability and continuous sections
items.statement: dim_κ Z¹(Γ, V) = h¹ + dim V − h⁰, and for Γ = Γ_F, dim Z¹(Γ_F, V) = dim V([F:ℚ_p] + 1) + h⁰(Γ_F, V^*(1)) = dim V([F:ℚ_p] + 1) + h²(Γ_F, V) (Lemma 3.1); D^□_{ρ,G} is pro-represented by a complete local noetherian Λ-algebra R^□_{ρ,G} with tangent space Z¹(Γ, ad ρ) (Lemma 3.2); continuous open surjections of locally profinite groups have continuous sections, G(A) is locally profinite for A ∈ 𝔄_Λ and surjections G(A) → G(B) have continuous sections (Lemmas 3.3–3.5).
items.note: Framed representability for GL_d is planned in R08.1; the G-valued statements are its generalisation.

items.name: Local Tate duality and the Euler–Poincaré formula over finite and local coefficient fields
items.statement: For V a continuous representation of Γ_F on a finite-dimensional vector space over a finite or local O-field κ (including local fields of characteristic p), local Tate duality H²(Γ_F, V) ≅ H⁰(Γ_F, V^*(1))^* and the Euler–Poincaré formula h⁰ − h¹ + h² = −[F:ℚ_p] dim V hold ([7, Theorem 3.4.1]).
items.note: Finite and p-adic coefficients are planned (Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 5, ArithmeticGaloisDuality D7); the BIP23 extraction routed the local-field-of-characteristic-p case to D7 as a source, and this item joins it.

items.name: Proposition 3.6 and Corollary 3.8: presentations of R^□_{ρ,G}
items.statement: Let φ : G → H be a morphism of smooth affine O-groups with G^0 → H^0 smooth and surjective, and ad^{0,φ} = ker(ad ρ → ad φ∘ρ). Then R^□_{ρ,G} ≅ R^□_{φ∘ρ,H}⟦x_1, …, x_r⟧/(f_1, …, f_t) with r = dim Z¹(Γ, ad^{0,φ}ρ), t = h²(Γ, ad^{0,φ}ρ), and for Γ = Γ_F, r − t = (dim G_κ − dim H_κ)([F:ℚ_p] + 1). With H trivial: R^□_{ρ,G} ≅ Λ⟦x_1..x_r⟧/(f_1..f_s), r − s = dim G_κ([F:ℚ_p] + 1). Applied to G → G/G′ (Remark 3.7).
items.note: Generalises BIP23 Proposition 4.3 (G = GL_d, H = GL_1, φ = det); over local κ the obstruction is realised by a continuous 2-cocycle using the continuous sections of Lemma 3.5 (Conrad's modularity lifting seminar [17], Lecture 6).

items.name: Lemma 3.9: complete intersection and flatness from dimension counts
items.statement: If A is a complete local noetherian complete intersection O-algebra with residue field k and B = A⟦x_1..x_r⟧/(f_1..f_t) with dim B ≤ dim A + r − t, then B is a complete intersection of dimension dim A + r − t; if moreover dim k ⊗_A B ≤ r − t then B is A-flat with dim k ⊗_A B = r − t (miracle flatness).
items.note: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3 plans 'the exact complete-intersection criteria used in patching' (the BIP23 extraction recorded its version as planned there).

items.name: Lemmas 3.10–3.11: coefficient extension and completion at characteristic-zero or local points
items.statement: For κ′/κ finite, Λ′ ⊗_Λ R^□_{G,ρ} ≅ R^□_{G,ρ′} (Lemma 3.10). If ρ : Γ → G(κ) has image in G(O_κ) with reduction ρ̄, then R^□_{G,ρ} is the completion of Λ ⊗_O R^□_{G,ρ̄} at the kernel 𝔮 of Λ ⊗ R^□_{G,ρ̄} → κ (Lemma 3.11; Kisin [36, Prop. 9.5], Böckle–Juschka [7, Thm 3.3.1] for GL_d).
items.note: R08.1 asks to relate local rings to residue-field extension.

items.name: Corollary 3.12 and Proposition 3.13: central quotients
items.statement: Let H = G/Z with Z a flat closed subgroup of Z(G^0), normal in G. If Z is finite étale then R^□_H = R^□_G. If Z is a torus with Z ∩ G′ étale, then R^□_{G/G′} ⊗̂_{R^□_{H/H′}} R^□_H ≅ R^□_G.
items.note: R08.1 plans 'the effect of fixing the determinant'; these are its G-valued analogues.

items.name: Corollary 3.14 and Proposition 3.16: dimensions under central quotients
items.statement: For Γ = Γ_F and κ finite: in the setting of Proposition 3.13, dim R^□_G/ϖ = dim R^□_H/ϖ + ([F:ℚ_p] + 1)(dim G_k − dim H_k) (Corollary 3.14, using [PQ25, Corollary 9.9]); if Z is finite connected diagonalisable then R^□_H → R^□_G is finite (Lemma 3.15) and dim R^□_H/ϖ = dim R^□_G/ϖ (Proposition 3.16).
items.note: PQ25 = Paškūnas–Quast, On local Galois deformation rings: generalised tori, Forum Math. Sigma 13 (2025) e45, a prerequisite not yet extracted; its results are stated inputs here.

items.name: Continuity via algebra (Lemmas 4.1–4.5)
items.statement: Let R be noetherian profinite, R → A, X = Spec B affine of finite type over O. Polynomials map finitely generated R-submodules of Aⁿ continuously into finitely generated R-submodules (Lemma 4.1). For a profinite set S and f : S → X(A) the following are equivalent: coordinatewise f lands in finitely generated R-submodules continuously; for all closed immersions τ : X ↪ 𝔸ⁿ, τ∘f lands continuously in a finitely generated R-submodule of Aⁿ; for one such τ (Lemma 4.2). The conditions are stable under morphisms, products and change R → R′ (Lemmas 4.3–4.5).
items.note: After Conrad's topologisation of X(A) [18].

items.name: R-condensed maps and representations (Definitions 4.7, 4.10)
items.statement: f : S → X(A) is R-condensed if it underlies a map of condensed sets S → X(A_disc ⊗_{R_disc} R) (A_disc ⊗_{R_disc} R an ind-profinite, quasi-separated 'relatively discrete' module, Lemma 4.6); this is equivalent to the conditions of Lemma 4.2 (Lemma 4.8) and implies continuity for topological R-algebras A (Lemma 4.9). ρ : Γ → G(A) is R-condensed if it is so as a map of sets; then it lifts uniquely to a homomorphism of condensed groups Γ → G(A_disc ⊗_{R_disc} R) (Lemma 4.12).
items.locator: §4.2–4.3, Lemma 4.6, Definition 4.7, Lemmas 4.8, 4.9, Definition 4.10, Remark 4.11, Lemma 4.12, pp. 27–28
items.note: Inspired by Fargues–Scholze's ℓ ≠ p definition [28, VIII]. Remark 4.11: one may take the embedding criterion as the definition.

items.name: Lemmas 4.13–4.16: properties of R-condensed representations
items.statement: ρ is R-condensed iff its restriction to an open subgroup is (Lemma 4.13); for Γ topologically finitely generated and A a filtered union of closed R-subalgebras with R-finite open subalgebras, ρ is continuous iff R-condensed (Lemma 4.14); an R-condensed ρ factors through a closed subgroup H iff the topological generators land in H(A) (Lemma 4.15); composition with φ : G → H preserves R-condensedness, and conversely for closed immersions (Lemma 4.16).

items.name: Determinant laws, R^ps_{GL_d} and the Cayley–Hamilton quotient
items.statement: For τ : G ↪ GL_d (existence: SGA3 VI_B 11.11.1), D is the continuous determinant law of (τ∘ρ̄)^lin on k⟦Γ⟧; R^ps_{GL_d} its universal deformation ring (Chenevier [15, §3.1]) with universal D^u on R^ps⟦Γ⟧; CH(D^u) the Cayley–Hamilton ideal and E^u = R^ps⟦Γ⟧/CH(D^u); homomorphisms of Cayley–Hamilton algebras E^u → M_d(A).
items.note: IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.0 plans determinants and IHG.1 the Cayley–Hamilton quotient (as recorded by the BIP23 extraction).

items.name: E^u is a finitely generated R^ps-module (Wang-Erickson) and Lemma 5.1
items.statement: Since Γ satisfies Mazur's p-finiteness, E^u is a finitely generated R^ps_{GL_d}-module and CH(D^u) is closed ([62, Proposition 3.6]); hence R^ps[Γ] → E^u is surjective (Lemma 5.1).
items.note: Wang-Erickson, Math. Ann. 371 (2018); the BIP23 extraction routed this finiteness to IHG.1 as a source, and this item joins it.

items.name: Lemmas 5.2, 5.4: Wang-Erickson's space of generic matrices X^gen_{GL_d}
items.statement: For ρ : Γ → GL_d(A) with det∘ρ^lin = D^u|_A, the following are equivalent: ρ^lin extends to R^ps⟦Γ⟧; it factors through E^u; ρ is R^ps-condensed; ρ is R-condensed (R noetherian profinite); then E^u → M_d(A) is Cayley–Hamilton (Lemma 5.2). X^gen_{GL_d} (such ρ, Definition 5.3) is in bijection with Cayley–Hamilton homomorphisms E^u → M_d(A), hence represented by a finitely generated R^ps-algebra A^gen_{GL_d} (the X^gen of BIP23), and its points over topological R^ps-algebras are continuous (Lemma 5.4).
items.note: Representability is BIP23 Lemma 3.1 (Procesi), routed to IHG.1 by that extraction; the condensed characterisation is new here.

items.name: Definition 5.7: the scheme X^{gen,τ}_G
items.statement: Fix a topologically finitely generated quotient Γ ↠ Q with the same R^ps and E^u (Lemma 5.5) and γ_1, …, γ_N generating Q densely and spanning k ⊗ E^u (so X^gen_{GL_d} ↪ GL_d^N × X^ps is closed, Lemma 5.6). X^{gen,τ}_G := X^gen_{GL_d} ×_{GL_d^N} G^N, a closed subscheme of G^N × X^ps (Remark 5.8), whose A-points are the ρ : Γ → G(A) with τ∘ρ ∈ X^gen_{GL_d}(A) (Lemma 5.10), independent of Q and the γ_i (Remark 5.11); for dim R^ps/𝔭 ≤ 1 its κ(𝔭)-bar points are the continuous ρ with det∘(τ∘ρ)^lin = D^u ⊗ κ(𝔭) (Lemma 5.12); the Zariski closure of ρ_x(Γ) is the closed subgroup generated by the ρ_x(γ_i) (Lemma 5.13).

items.name: Proposition 5.16 and Lemma 5.17: completions of X^{gen,τ}_G are framed deformation rings
items.statement: Closed points x of Y (the preimage of the closed point of X^ps) have finite residue fields over k, closed points of X^gen[1/p] finite extensions of L, closed points of X̄^gen ∖ Y local fields of characteristic p. D^□_{ρ,G}(A) ≅ D^□_{τ∘ρ,GL_d}(A) ×_{GL_d^N(A)} G^N(A) (Lemma 5.14); the completion of Λ ⊗ A^{gen,τ}_G at x is R^□_{ρ_x,G} (Proposition 5.16); Ô_{X,x} ≅ R^□_{G,ρ_x} for x ∈ X[1/p] or x ∈ Y and Ô_{X̄,x}⟦T⟧ ≅ R^□_{G,ρ_x} for x ∈ X̄ ∖ Y; O_{X,x} is a complete intersection iff R^□_{G,ρ_x} is (Lemma 5.17).
items.note: Uses BIP23 Proposition 3.33 and Lemmas 3.36, 3.37.

items.name: Lemma 5.15: completing a quotient by a finitely generated ideal
items.statement: Let (A, 𝔪) be a local ring, possibly non-noetherian, whose 𝔪-adic completion Â is noetherian, and I ⊂ A finitely generated. Then the completion of A/I is Â/IÂ.
items.note: General commutative algebra of the kind the BIP23 extraction routed to DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra.

items.name: Cotner's finiteness theorem for character varieties
items.statement: Let S be locally noetherian and f : H → G a finite morphism of generalised reductive smooth affine S-group schemes. Then Hᴺ//H → Gᴺ//G is finite (Vinberg in characteristic 0, Martin in characteristic p, Cotner [21] in general); hence Hᴺ//H^0 → Gᴺ//G^0 is finite (Corollary 6.3).
items.note: Cotner, IMRN 2024, 11540–11548; a prerequisite. Not planned in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 6.4 and Corollary 6.5: finiteness of GIT quotients
items.statement: X^{git,τ}_G := X^{gen,τ}_G//G^0 (and its special fibre) is finite over X^ps_{GL_d}; for a closed generalised reductive H ⊂ G (or G_k), X^{git}_H → X^{git}_G is finite. The special-fibre GIT quotient maps finitely and homeomorphically to the special fibre of X^git (Seshadri, Remark 6.1).
items.note: Seshadri [57] Theorems 2, 3.

items.name: Proposition 6.6: continuous representations are conjugate into G(O_κ′)
items.statement: For κ a local O-field and ρ : Γ_F → G(κ) continuous there are a finite extension κ′/κ and g ∈ G^0(κ′) with gρ(γ)g^{−1} ∈ G(O_κ′) for all γ.
items.note: Cotner [21, Lemma 4.3].

items.name: Proposition 6.7 to Corollary 6.11: closed orbits and G-semisimplicity
items.statement: For a geometric point x of X^{gen,τ}_G with H the Zariski closure of ρ_x(Γ_F): G^0·x closed in its fibre over X^git ⇔ G·x closed ⇔ H strongly reductive in G (Martin) ⇔ ρ_x G-completely reducible (Proposition 6.7; Richardson [51, Thm 16.4], Bate–Martin–Röhrle [3, Thm 3.1]). Each geometric fibre over X^git has a unique closed G^0-orbit (Lemma 6.8), the one of the G-semisimplification (Proposition 6.9); two points have the same image in X^git iff same G-semisimplification (Corollary 6.10); for G split, each fibre contains a point with image in an R-Levi L ⊃ T defined over O on which it is L-irreducible, unique up to G^0-conjugacy (Corollary 6.11).

items.name: The components X^{gen,τ}_{G,ρ̄^ss} and R^{git}_{G,ρ̄^ss}
items.statement: R^{git,τ}_G = (A^{gen,τ}_G)^{G^0} ≅ R_1 × ⋯ × R_n with R_j complete local noetherian R^ps-algebras (finite over R^ps_{GL_d}), giving a G^0-equivariant decomposition of X^{gen,τ}_G into connected components (Lemma 6.12); X^{gen,τ}_{G,ρ̄^ss} is the one containing ρ̄, R^{git,τ}_{G,ρ̄^ss} its invariant ring (residue field k). A geometric point over the closed point of X^ps lies in it iff its G-semisimplification is ρ̄^ss (Lemma 6.13); after an unramified extension the components correspond to G^0(k̄)-classes of G-cr ρ^ss with determinant law D (Remark 6.14).

items.name: V. Lafforgue's G-pseudocharacters over O, for disconnected G
items.statement: A G-pseudocharacter Θ of Γ over a commutative O-algebra A is a sequence of O-algebra maps Θ_n : O[Gⁿ]^{G^0} → Map(Γⁿ, A) compatible with maps ζ : {1..m} → {1..n} and with ĝ(g_1..g_{n+1}) = f(g_1..g_n g_{n+1}); PC^Γ_G(A) the set, with specialisation along A → B, pushforward φ∘Θ along φ : G → H, continuous pseudocharacters cPC^Γ_G(A); PC_{G_{O′}} = PC_G for O-algebras O′ ([35, I.4.18], [50, Prop. 3.21]).
items.note: The BHKT19 extraction routed Ĝ-pseudocharacters to IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.0 as a source; this is the O-integral, non-connected version. Quast, Deformations of G-valued pseudocharacters, Peking Math. J. (2026) [50], a prerequisite not yet extracted.

items.name: Deformations of G-pseudocharacters and Quast's theorems
items.statement: For Θ̄ ∈ cPC^Γ_G(κ), D_Θ̄(A) = {Θ ∈ cPC^Γ_G(A) : Θ ⊗ κ = Θ̄} on 𝔄_Λ is pro-represented by R^ps_G (Definition 7.2); for Γ topologically finitely generated R^ps_G is complete local noetherian ([50, Thm A, Thm 5.7]); PC^Γ_G is representable by an affine scheme ([50, Thm 3.19]); over an algebraically closed field every G-pseudocharacter comes from a G-semisimple ρ, unique up to G^0-conjugacy, continuously so in the topological case ([50, Thms 3.7, 3.8]).
items.note: The BHKT19 extraction routed the reconstruction theorem over algebraically closed fields to IHG.1 as a source. Quast, Deformations of G-valued pseudocharacters, Peking Math. J. (2026) [50], a prerequisite not yet extracted.

items.name: Emerson–Morel: comparison of pseudocharacter notions
items.statement: For G = GL_d, G-pseudocharacters are equivalent to Chenevier's d-dimensional determinant laws ([25]); for the free group F_N and R^ps[1/p], R[PC^{F_N}_G][1/p] ≅ R[Rep^{F_N,□}_G]^{G^0}[1/p] ([25, Prop. 2.11(i)]).
items.locator: §1.3, p. 5; §7, p. 39; proof of Lemma 7.5, p. 42 (cited)
items.note: Emerson–Morel, arXiv 2310.03869; a prerequisite. Belongs with determinants and pseudocharacters in IHG.0–IHG.1.

items.name: Lemmas 8.8–8.9: pseudocharacters of products
items.statement: PC^Γ_{G_1 × G_2} ≅ PC^Γ_{G_1} × PC^Γ_{G_2} and likewise for continuous ones (since O[(G_1×G_2)^m]^{G^0} = O[G_1^m]^{G_1^0} ⊗ O[G_2^m]^{G_2^0}); hence R^ps_G ≅ R^ps_{G_1} ⊗̂_O R^ps_{G_2}.

items.name: Proposition 7.4 (= Proposition 1.8), Lemma 7.5 and Corollary 7.6
items.statement: The G-pseudocharacter of the universal representation is continuous over R^{git}_{G,ρ̄^ss} (Lemma 7.3), giving ν : X^{git,τ}_{G,ρ̄^ss} → X^ps_G, a finite universal homeomorphism (Proposition 7.4); ν[1/p] is a closed immersion (Lemma 7.5), hence an isomorphism on reduced schemes, and an isomorphism if X^ps_G[1/p] is reduced (Corollary 7.6). By [47] ν[1/p] is an isomorphism (Remark 7.7).
items.locator: §1.4.1, Proposition 1.8, p. 7; §7.3, Lemma 7.3, Proposition 7.4, Lemma 7.5, Corollary 7.6, Remark 7.7, pp. 40–42
items.note: The GL_d analogue is Wang-Erickson's adequate homeomorphism X^gen//GL_d → X^ps (a stated input of the BIP23 Part II).

items.name: Proposition 8.3 and Corollary 8.4: intrinsic description, independent of τ
items.statement: For an R^ps_G-algebra A, X^{gen,τ}_{G,ρ̄^ss}(A) is the set of ρ : Γ → G(A) with Θ_ρ equal to the specialisation of Θ^u and ρ R^ps_G-condensed (equivalently R-condensed for a noetherian profinite R^ps-algebra R → A, or (τ∘ρ)^lin factoring through R^ps_G ⊗ E^u) (Lemmas 8.1, 8.2, Proposition 8.3). Hence A^{gen,τ}_{G,ρ̄^ss} does not depend on τ (Corollary 8.4); write X^gen_{G,ρ̄^ss}, X^git_{G,ρ̄^ss}.
items.note: Γ_F is topologically finitely generated (Jannsen [34, Satz 3.6]); [46] extends §8 to Mazur's finiteness.

items.name: Propositions 8.5–8.7 and 8.10: functoriality in G, finite maps, products
items.statement: A homomorphism φ : G → H gives X^gen_{G,ρ̄^ss} → X^gen_{H,(φ∘ρ̄^ss)^ss}, ρ ↦ φ∘ρ (Proposition 8.5); if φ is finite then X^ps_G → X^ps_H and X^gen_G → X^gen_H are finite (Propositions 8.6, 8.7); X^gen_{G_1×G_2} ≅ (X^gen_{G_1} × X^gen_{G_2}) ×_{X^ps_{G_1} × X^ps_{G_2}} X^ps_G (Proposition 8.10).
items.note: Footnote 8 (the referee's point): the target is X^gen_{H,(φ∘ρ̄^ss)^ss}, since φ∘ρ̄^ss need not be H-semisimple.

items.name: Lemmas 8.11–8.12: restriction to open subgroups
items.statement: For Γ′ ⊂ Γ open, restriction gives a finite morphism X^{ps,Γ}_G → X^{ps,Γ′}_G (BIP23 Lemma A.3 for GL_d) and a morphism of finite type X^{gen,Γ}_{G,ρ̄^ss} → X^{gen,Γ′}_{G,ρ̄^ss}.

items.name: Lemmas 9.1–9.4: trimming the component group
items.statement: For a closed H ⊂ G with H^0 = G^0 and (π_G∘ρ̄^ss)(Γ) ⊂ (H/H^0)(k), X^git_{H,ρ̄^ss} = X^git_{G,ρ̄^ss} and X^gen_{H,ρ̄^ss} = X^gen_{G,ρ̄^ss}; H may be chosen with π_H∘ρ̄^ss surjective (Lemma 9.2). The scheme-theoretic images X^git_{HG} satisfy dim X^git_{HG} ≤ dim X^git_H (41), and after an unramified extension X^git_{H,ρ̄^ss} and X^gen_{H,ρ̄^ss} decompose into X^{git/gen}_{H_i,ρ_i} with π_{H_i}∘ρ_i surjective (Lemma 9.4).

items.name: The strata U_{LG}, V_{LG} and the absolutely G-irreducible locus
items.statement: For G^0 split with maximal split torus T and R-Levis L ⊃ T: U_{LG} = X^git_{LG} ∖ (pts ∪ ⋃_{T ⊂ M ⊊ L} X^git_{MG}), V_{LG} its preimage in X^gen; X^gen = Y ∪ ⋃_L V_{LG} (42). A geometric point x is G-stable if G·x is closed and dim Z_G(x) = dim Z(G) (Definition 9.5). For x ∉ Y: x ∈ V_{GG} ⇔ ρ_x G-irreducible ⇔ its Zariski closure H is G-irreducible ⇔ x is G-stable, and then H is reductive with dim Z_G(H) = dim Z(G) (Proposition 9.7). If π_G∘ρ̄^ss is surjective, V_{GG,ρ̄^ss} is the absolutely G-irreducible locus (Definition 9.12).
items.locator: §9.2, (42), Definition 9.5, Remark 9.6, Proposition 9.7, Definition 9.12, Remark 9.13, pp. 48–50
items.note: Example 9.14 (p > 2, the normaliser of the diagonal torus of GL_2, E/F quadratic): without surjectivity the naive locus can be empty; Remark 9.15 records the referee's alternative via G-normalisers of parabolics of G^0.

items.name: Corollaries 9.8–9.10 and Lemma 9.11: dimensions over the absolutely irreducible locus
items.statement: If X̄^git_{HG} ∩ Ū_{LG} ≠ ∅ for H ⊂ L_{k′} generalised reductive then dim Z(H) ≤ dim Z(L_k) (Corollary 9.8). Fibres of X^gen over points of U_{GG} have dimension dim G_k − dim Z(G_k) (Corollary 9.9), so preimages V of locally closed U ⊂ U_{GG} have dim V = dim U + dim G_k − dim Z(G_k) (Corollary 9.10). If π_G∘ρ̄^ss is surjective and some stratum for L is non-empty then L/L^0 ≅ G/G^0, dim L = dim G forces L = G, and L ≠ G forces dim N_k ≥ 1 for the unipotent radical N (Lemma 9.11).
items.note: Martin [42, Lemma 6.2]; Seshadri [57, Thm 3].

items.name: Proposition 10.1 and Corollaries 10.2–10.3 (= Proposition 1.9): codimension of reductive subgroups
items.statement: Let G be generalised reductive over an algebraically closed κ and H a closed reductive subgroup. Either H ⊇ G′ or dim G′ − dim(H ∩ G′) ≥ 2; in the second case dim G − dim H ≥ 2. If a finite-dimensional representation V has V^{G′} = 0 and V^H ≠ 0 then dim G − dim H ≥ 2.
items.note: Proof via Borel subgroups and opposite unipotent radicals (a simplification suggested by Cotner and the referee).

items.name: Lemmas 10.4–10.5 (= Lemma 1.10): no invariants in (Lie G′_sc)^*
items.statement: If π_1(G′) is étale then ((Lie G′)^*)^{G′} = 0; in general the G′-invariants of (Lie G′_sc)^* vanish (the statement fails in small characteristic without the dual).
items.note: First for SL_2 (Sym² of the standard representation, or a non-split extension in characteristic 2), then root by root.

items.name: Lemma 10.6, Corollary 10.7: invariants in (Lie U)^*
items.statement: For an R-parabolic with R-Levi L and unipotent radical U and a closed reductive H ⊂ L with ((Lie U)^*)^H ≠ 0: dim L − dim H ≥ 2, or dim L − dim H = 1 and dim ((Lie U)^*)^H = 1; in particular ((Lie U)^*)^{L^0} = 0.
items.note: Example 10.8: G = G_1 × SL_2, H = G_1 × {1} realises case (ii).

items.name: Proposition 11.1 and Corollary 11.2: R-Levis of codimension 2
items.statement: If dim U = 1 and L/L^0 → G/G^0 is an isomorphism, then the image Ḡ of G in Aut(G^0) is G_1 × PGL_2 with G_1^0 semisimple, P̄ ≅ G_1 × B_2, L̄ ≅ G_1 × T_2, Ū ≅ U_2; hence Lie G′_sc ≅ Lie SL_2 ⊕ Lie (G′_1)_sc as G-representations.
items.note: Via Aut(G^0) ≅ G^0 ⋊ Θ (Conrad [19, Thm 7.1.9]).

items.name: Lemmas 11.3–11.4 and Proposition 11.5: non-speciality near codimension-2 Levis
items.statement: Let H_0 = p_2^{−1}(μ_{p−1}) ⊂ G (p_2 : G → Ḡ → PGL_2, μ_{p−1} ⊂ T_2 ≅ 𝔾_m via α). H_0 is generalised reductive with dim Z(H_0) < dim Z(L) (Lemma 11.3). For ρ : Γ_F → B_2(κ) with character ψ = α∘ρ, if ψ ≠ ω^{±1} (ω = χ_cyc ⊗ κ) and ρ(Γ_F) lies in no maximal split torus of B_2, then h⁰(Γ_F, (Lie SL_2)^*(1)) = 0 (Lemma 11.4). For κ of characteristic p: if ρ : Γ_F → P(κ) lies in no R-Levi of P, its G-semisimplification is not in H_0, and h⁰(Γ_F, (Lie(G′_1)_sc)^*(1)) = 0, then h⁰(Γ_F, (Lie G′_sc)^*(1)) = 0 (Proposition 11.5).
items.note: Lemma 11.4 extends BIP23 Lemma 4.2 to all F. Proposition 11.5 is stated for any algebraically closed κ but is false in characteristic 0; the item adds char κ = p, the case of its only use (Proposition 14.5, on the special fibre). Source issue E1.

items.name: Lemmas 12.1–12.7 and Proposition 12.8: the unipotent fibre spaces X^gen_{P,ρ}
items.statement: For 𝔭 ⊂ R^ps_G with dim R^ps/𝔭 ≤ 1 and y the corresponding point, a unique point of X^git lies over ȳ and the fibres agree on reduced schemes (Lemma 12.1); for G split there is an L-irreducible ρ : Γ_F → L(κ̄) in the closed G^0-orbit of the fibre. For an R-parabolic P with R-Levi L and unipotent radical U, X^gen_{P,ρ} (R^ps-condensed ρ′ : Γ_F → P(A) with ρ′ ≡ ρ mod U(A), Definition 12.3) is a closed subscheme of X^gen_{G,y} (Lemma 12.4) with tangent space Z¹(Γ_F, (Lie U)_κ) at ρ (Lemma 12.5), κ-points the continuous such lifts (Lemma 12.6) and {ρ} its unique closed 𝔾_m-orbit (Lemma 12.7); dim X^gen_{P,ρ} ≤ dim U + dim U[F:ℚ_p] + h⁰(Γ_F, (Lie U)^*_κ(1)) (Proposition 12.8).

items.name: Proposition 12.15: fibre dimension bound via the defect
items.statement: Every point of X^gen_{G,y} is G^0-conjugate into some X^gen_{P,ρ} with R-Levi L (Lemma 12.9). With the defect δ(y) = max_P h⁰(Γ_F, (Lie U)^*_κ(1)) over the finitely many R-parabolics with R-Levi L (Definition 12.10; depends only on y, Remark 12.12), δ(y) ≤ ½(dim G_κ − dim L_κ) (Lemma 12.14) and dim X^gen_{G,y} ≤ dim G_κ − dim Z(L_κ) + ½(dim G_κ − dim L_κ)[F:ℚ_p] + δ(y).
items.locator: §12, Lemma 12.9, Definition 12.10, Remarks 12.11–12.13, 12.16, Lemma 12.14, Proposition 12.15, pp. 58–59

items.name: Corollary 12.18: the closed fibre Y_{ρ̄^ss}
items.statement: If dim G_k > 1 then dim G_k(1 + [F:ℚ_p]) − dim Y_{ρ̄^ss} ≥ [F:ℚ_p] dim L_k + dim Z(L_k) ≥ [F:ℚ_p] + 1, with equality only when dim G_k − dim L_k = 2 and L is ρ̄^ss-compatible; otherwise the difference is ≥ 2[F:ℚ_p] + 1. (An R-Levi of dimension 1 forces G^0 = SL_2 or PGL_2, Lemma 12.17.)

items.name: The induction hypothesis (DIM) and ρ̄^ss-compatible pairs
items.statement: (DIM) for (H, ρ_1): dim X̄^git_{H,ρ_1} ≤ dim Z(H) + [F:ℚ_p] dim H, for H generalised reductive over a finite extension of k and ρ_1 H-semisimple with π_H∘ρ_1 surjective. (H, ρ_1) is ρ̄^ss-compatible if H ⊂ G_k is closed and the G-semisimplification of ρ_1 is G^0(k̄)-conjugate to ρ̄^ss. Non-empty X̄^git_{LG,ρ̄^ss} makes L_k compatible, of smaller dimension if L ≠ G (Lemma 13.1); closures of locally closed U ⊂ X^git ∖ {*} and of open G^0-invariant V ⊂ X ∖ Y gain one dimension (Lemmas 13.2, 13.3); dim X^gen = max over closed x ∈ Y of dim R^□_{ρ_x} (Lemma 13.4).
items.note: (DIM) holds when H^0 is a torus by [PQ25, Theorem 9.3(3)]. PQ25 = Paškūnas–Quast, On local Galois deformation rings: generalised tori, Forum Math. Sigma 13 (2025) e45, a prerequisite not yet extracted; its results are stated inputs here.

items.name: Proposition 13.5 and Corollaries 13.6–13.7: codimension bounds from (DIM)
items.statement: For H ⊂ L_{k′} closed reductive (H ≠ G if L = G), U open in X̄^git_{HG} ∩ Ū_{LG,ρ̄^ss}, V its preimage and Z = V̄, if (DIM) holds for compatible pairs of smaller dimension then dim G_k([F:ℚ_p] + 1) − dim Z ≥ (dim L_k − dim H)[F:ℚ_p] + dim N_k[F:ℚ_p] − δ(U); hence ≥ (dim L_k − dim H)[F:ℚ_p] (Corollary 13.6), and for L ≠ G with δ(U) ≤ dim L_k − dim H, ≥ dim N_k[F:ℚ_p] ≥ 1, ≥ 2 unless F = ℚ_p and dim N_k = 1 (Corollary 13.7).

items.name: W-special loci (Lemma 13.8, Definition 13.9)
items.statement: For W a representation of G on a free R-module of finite rank and ρ : Γ_F → G(A), A noetherian: X_{W,j} = {x ∈ Spec A : dim_{κ(x)} (W_x(1))^{Γ_F} ≥ j+1} is closed (reduced structure) — via the support of W̌(A)/M, M generated by χ_cyc(g)^{−1}g·ℓ − ℓ, and upper semicontinuity. X_{W,0} is the W-special locus, its complement the W-non-special locus. In characteristic p, x ∈ X_{W,j} forces dim W_x^{H^0} ≥ j+1 for H the Zariski closure of ρ_x(Γ_F) (Lemma 13.10).

items.name: Propositions 13.11–13.16: invariance and structure of special loci
items.statement: On X^gen_{G,ρ̄^ss} (and its special and generic fibres) the W-special loci of level j are G^0-invariant, also inside closed G^0-invariant X′ (Proposition 13.11, Corollary 13.12); irreducible components of closed G^0-invariant Z meet Y with dim O_{Z′,x} = dim Z′ on Y and dim Z′ − 1 off Y (Lemma 13.13); dim Z[1/p] ≤ dim Z̄ and dim Z ≤ dim Z̄ + 1 (Proposition 13.14, Corollary 13.15). In the special fibre the image C_{W,j} of the W-special locus in X̄^git is closed and covered by finitely many X̄^git_{H_iG} with H_i reductive over a finite extension of k and dim W^{H_i^0} ≥ j+1; dim H_i ≤ dim G_k − 1 if W^{G^0} = 0 and ≤ dim G_k − 2 if W^{G′} = 0 (Proposition 13.16; Martin [42, Thm 10.3]).
items.note: Lemma 13.13 and Proposition 13.14 as BIP23 Lemmas 3.21, 3.23.

items.name: Propositions 13.17–13.18: codimension of the reducible strata and of the special absolutely irreducible locus
items.statement: Under (DIM) for smaller compatible pairs: for L ≠ G with U_{LG,ρ̄^ss} ≠ ∅, the closure Z_{LG} of V̄_{LG} has codimension ≥ min(2, dim N_k)[F:ℚ_p] ≥ 1 in dim G_k([F:ℚ_p] + 1), ≥ 2 unless F = ℚ_p and dim N_k = 1 (Proposition 13.17); the closure of the (Lie G′_sc)^*-special part of V̄_{GG} has codimension ≥ 2[F:ℚ_p] (Proposition 13.18).

items.name: Proposition 13.21 to Corollary 13.24: the non-special absolutely irreducible locus
items.statement: V^{n-spcl}_{GG,ρ̄^ss} is the complement of the (Lie G′_sc)^*-special locus in V_{GG,ρ̄^ss} (Definition 13.19; its special fibre is V̄^{n-spcl}, Remark 13.20). Under (DIM) for smaller pairs, its complement in X̄^gen has positive codimension and dim X̄^gen = dim V̄^{n-spcl} + 1 = dim X̄^git + dim G_k − dim Z(G_k) (Proposition 13.21). If π_1(G′) is étale or x is a characteristic-0 point, a closed point x ∉ Y lies in V^{n-spcl} iff ρ_x is absolutely G-irreducible with H²(Γ_F, ad⁰ρ_x) = 0 (Lemma 13.22), and V^{n-spcl} is O-flat of relative dimension dim G_k([F:ℚ_p] + 1) − 1 (Lemma 13.23); then dim X̄^gen = dim G_k([F:ℚ_p] + 1) and dim X̄^git = dim G_k[F:ℚ_p] + dim Z(G_k) (Corollary 13.24).
items.locator: §13.3, Definition 13.19, Remark 13.20, Proposition 13.21, Lemmas 13.22, 13.23, Corollary 13.24, pp. 66–68
items.note: Lemma 13.23 uses [PQ25, Corollary 9.5] (X^gen_{G/G′} is O-flat of relative dimension dim(G/G′)([F:ℚ_p] + 1)).

items.name: Proposition 13.25 and Theorem 13.26: the induction
items.statement: If (DIM) holds for all pairs of smaller dimension it holds for (G_k, ρ̄^ss) (Proposition 13.25: pass to G/Z(G′), G/Z(G^0) and, by Proposition 2.30, a cover G_3 with π_1(G_3^0) étale, using Corollaries 3.12, 3.14, Proposition 3.16). Hence (DIM) holds throughout, the complement of V̄^{n-spcl} has positive codimension, dim X̄^gen_{G,ρ̄^ss} = dim G_k([F:ℚ_p] + 1) and dim X̄^git_{G,ρ̄^ss} = dim G_k[F:ℚ_p] + dim Z(G_k) (Theorem 13.26).
items.note: The core of the paper (§1.4.2).

items.name: Corollaries 13.27–13.30: complete intersection at every point, flatness, density
items.statement: At every closed point x of X^gen_{G,ρ̄^ss} ∖ Y or of Y, R^□_{G,ρ_x} is Λ-flat of relative dimension dim G_k([F:ℚ_p] + 1) and a complete intersection, and R^□_{G,ρ_x}/ϖ is a complete intersection of that dimension in characteristic p (Corollary 13.27). X^gen_{G,ρ̄^ss} is O-flat, equidimensional of relative dimension d = dim G_k([F:ℚ_p] + 1) and lci; X̄^gen equidimensional of dimension d and lci (Corollary 13.28); likewise for closed generalised reductive H (Corollary 13.29); the non-special absolutely irreducible locus is dense in X^gen and X̄^gen (Corollary 13.30).
items.note: As BIP23 Corollaries 3.38, 3.40.

items.name: Corollaries 13.34–13.38: local fields, lifts to characteristic zero, density of non-special points
items.statement: The conclusions of Corollary 13.27 hold for ρ : Γ_F → G(κ) with κ a local field (Corollary 13.34). Every ρ̄ lifts to G(O′) for some finite L′/L (Corollary 13.35), and the lift may be chosen absolutely G-irreducible with H²(Γ_F, ad⁰ρ) = 0 (Corollary 13.38): the closed points of Spec R^□ ∖ {*} whose ρ_x is absolutely G-irreducible with H²(Γ_F, (Lie G′_sc)_x) = 0 are Zariski dense in Spec R^□ and in its special fibre (Corollary 13.36, Remark 13.37).
items.note: As BIP23 Proposition 3.55.

items.name: Lemma 14.2: dimension under dominant maps over a complete local base
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a dominant morphism of affine schemes of finite type over Spec R, R complete local noetherian over O with residue field k, such that every irreducible component of X meets the closed fibre X_s. Then dim Y ≤ dim X (the hypothesis is necessary: Spec ℚ_p → Spec ℤ_p, Remark 14.3).
items.note: Formalises an argument of BIP23 Proposition 3.8; uses BIP23 Lemmas 3.14, 3.18.

items.name: Proposition 14.4: the G^0-saturation of a smaller group's locus
items.statement: For H ⊂ G closed generalised reductive with X^gen_{H,ρ̄^ss} ≠ ∅, G^0 ×^{H^0} X^gen_H has dimension dim G^0 + dim X^gen_H − dim H^0 (81), dim X^gen_G − dim X^gen_H = (dim G − dim H)([F:ℚ_p] + 1) (82), and the scheme-theoretic image G^0·X^gen_{H,ρ̄^ss} (Definition 14.1) has codimension ≥ (dim G − dim H)[F:ℚ_p] (and likewise in the special fibre).

items.name: Proposition 14.5 and Theorem 14.6: codimension of the special locus
items.statement: For a ρ̄^ss-compatible R-Levi L with dim G − dim L = 2 there is a closed D̄_L ⊂ X̄^gen of codimension ≥ 1 + [F:ℚ_p] outside which points of V̄_{LG} are (Lie G′_sc)^*-non-special (Proposition 14.5). The (Lie G′_sc)^*-special locus has codimension ≥ 1 + [F:ℚ_p] in X^gen_{G,ρ̄^ss}, in its special fibre and in its generic fibre, and ≥ 2[F:ℚ_p] if no ρ̄^ss-compatible R-Levi has codimension 2 (Theorem 14.6).
items.note: Example 14.7 (G = GL_1 × GL_2): the bound is 2[F:ℚ_p] if ρ̄_2 is absolutely irreducible and 1 + [F:ℚ_p] if it is reducible.

items.name: Proposition 15.1 to Corollary 15.5: the fixed-partial-determinant space
items.statement: With Ḡ = G/Z_1: X^{gen,ψ_1}_{G,ρ̄^ss} → X^gen_{Ḡ,ρ̄^ss} is finite (Proposition 15.1), so dim X̄^{gen,ψ_1} ≤ dim Ḡ_k([F:ℚ_p] + 1) (Corollary 15.2), where dim Ḡ_k = dim(H_2)_k + dim G′_k (90); X^{gen,ψ_1}//Z_2G′ → X^git_Ḡ is finite (Corollary 15.3) and its ring is a finite product of complete local rings, local with residue field k if |(G/G^0)(k̄)| and |(Z_1 ∩ Z_2G′)(k̄)| are coprime (Corollary 15.4); irreducible components of closed Z_2G′-invariant subschemes meet Y^{ψ_1} with the expected local dimensions (Corollary 15.5).
items.note: For G = GL_d with fixed determinant this reduces to PGL_d, unlike BIP23 which untwists by characters.

items.name: Generalised tori (Paškūnas–Quast 2025) as used here
items.statement: With μ := (μ_{p^∞}(E) ⊗ M_2)^Δ of order p^m and L containing the p^m-th roots of unity: O⟦(Γ_E^{ab,p} ⊗ M_2)^Δ⟧ ≅ R^ps_{H_2,ψ̄_2} (93, [PQ25, Thm 9.3]); A^gen_{H_2,ψ̄_2^ss} ≅ R^ps[t_1^{±1}, …, t_s^{±1}], s = rank M_2 − rank M_2^Δ (94); O⟦(Γ_E^{ab,p} ⊗ M_2)^Δ⟧ ≅ O[μ]⟦x_1..x_r⟧, r = rank M_2[F:ℚ_p] + rank M_2^Δ ([PQ25, Cor. 8.8]), μ being the torsion via the Artin map; so A^gen ≅ O[μ]⟦x⟧[t^{±1}] with r + s = dim(H_2)_k([F:ℚ_p] + 1) (96). Also [PQ25, Cor. 9.5, 9.9] and the canonical free transitive action of X(μ) on components of X^ps_{H_2} ([PQ25, §7.4]).
items.note: PQ25 = Paškūnas–Quast, On local Galois deformation rings: generalised tori, Forum Math. Sigma 13 (2025) e45, a prerequisite not yet extracted; its results are stated inputs here. Local class field theory's Artin map is planned (Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 7).

items.name: Lemmas 15.6–15.11: characters of μ and the regular torus rings
items.statement: For χ ∈ X(μ) = Hom(μ, O^×) and A over X^ps_{H_2}, A_χ := A ⊗_{O[μ],χ} O; Z and Z_χ have the same reduced subscheme (Lemma 15.6); R^{□,χ}_{H_2,ψ_2} ≅ Λ⟦z_1..z_t⟧, t = dim(H_2)_k([F:ℚ_p] + 1) (Lemma 15.7); X^{gen,ψ_1}_{G/G′,ψ^ss} ≅ X^gen_{H_2,ψ_2^ss} (Lemma 15.8); every X^{gen,ψ_1,χ}_{G,ρ̄^ss} is non-empty (Lemma 15.9); R^{□,ψ_1,χ}_{G/G′,ψ} ≅ R^{□,χ}_{H_2,ψ_2} ≅ Λ⟦z_1..z_t⟧ (Lemma 15.10); completions of X^{gen,ψ_1,χ} are the rings R^{□,ψ_1,χ}_{G,ρ_x} (Lemma 15.11).

items.name: Corollaries 15.12–15.15: complete intersection with fixed partial determinant
items.statement: R^{□,ψ_1,χ}_{G,ρ_x} ≅ Λ⟦z_1..z_t, x_1..x_r⟧/(f_1..f_s) with r − s = dim G′_k([F:ℚ_p] + 1) (100) is Λ-flat of relative dimension dim Ḡ_k([F:ℚ_p] + 1) and a complete intersection, and so is its reduction mod ϖ (Corollary 15.12; also for R^{□,ψ_1}, Remark 15.13); X^{gen,ψ_1,χ}_{G,ρ̄^ss} is O-flat of relative dimension dim Ḡ_k([F:ℚ_p] + 1) and lci, and its special fibre lci of that dimension (Corollary 15.14); its (Lie G′_sc)^*-special loci have codimension ≥ 1 + [F:ℚ_p] (≥ 2[F:ℚ_p] without a compatible codimension-2 R-Levi) (Corollary 15.15).

items.name: Lemmas 15.16–15.17 and Theorems 15.18–15.19: Serre's criterion
items.statement: The (Lie G′_sc)^*_L-non-special locus of X^{gen,ψ_1,χ}[1/p] is regular, and if π_1(G′) is étale so are those of X^{gen,ψ_1,χ} and its special fibre (Lemma 15.16); with c(ρ̄^ss) = 2[F:ℚ_p] − 1 if no ρ̄^ss-compatible R-Levi has codimension 2 and [F:ℚ_p] otherwise, these schemes are regular in codimension c(ρ̄^ss) (Lemma 15.17). If π_1(G′) is étale, X^{gen,ψ_1,χ} and its special fibre are normal, and integral if |(G/G^0)(k̄)| and |(Z_1 ∩ Z_2G′)(k̄)| are coprime (Theorem 15.18); X^{gen,ψ_1,χ}[1/p] is always normal (Theorem 15.19).

items.name: Corollaries 15.20–15.22: normal domains and factoriality of the deformation rings
items.statement: If π_1(G′) is étale, at closed points x of X̄^{gen,ψ_1,χ} ∖ Y or of Y, R^{□,ψ_1,χ}_{G,ρ_x} and R^{□,ψ_1,χ}_{G,ρ_x}/ϖ are normal domains regular in codimension c(ρ̄^ss) (Corollary 15.20); at closed points of the generic fibre R^{□,ψ_1,χ}_{G,ρ_x} is a normal domain regular in codimension c(ρ̄^ss) without assumption on π_1(G′) (Corollary 15.21); if [F:ℚ_p] ≥ 3, or [F:ℚ_p] = 2 without a compatible codimension-2 R-Levi, these rings are factorial (Corollary 15.22).

items.name: Commutative algebra inputs: Serre's criterion, excellence, parafactoriality, miracle flatness
items.statement: Serre's criterion for normality (R_1 + S_2) with Cohen–Macaulayness of complete intersections; finitely generated algebras over complete local noetherian rings are excellent, and completions of excellent local rings regular in codimension i are regular in codimension i ([43, Thm 23.9], [59, Tag 07QW]); Grothendieck's parafactoriality: a complete intersection regular in codimension 3 is factorial ([14]); miracle flatness ([43, Thm 23.1]); invariants of normal domains under reductive groups are normal ([12, Prop. 6.4.1]).
items.note: The BIP23 extraction routed Serre's criterion, excellence and parafactoriality to DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra; this item joins them.

items.name: Section 15.6: labelling the irreducible components
items.statement: The bijection between components and X(μ) is non-canonical in general (it depends on α in (93)). If H_2 ≅ H_2^0 ⋊ Δ, the Teichmüller section of H_2^0(O) ↠ H_2^0(k) gives a canonical minimally ramified lift σ∘ψ̄_2 and so a canonical component; equivalently a Q̄_p-point with ψ_2(γ) = (Φ(γ), γ|_E) defines a class in H¹(Γ_F, H_2^0(Q̄_p)) ≅ Hom_cont((Γ_F^{ab,p} ⊗ M_2)^Δ, Q̄_p^×) (Langlands' argument for tori), whose restriction to μ labels the component.
items.note: [PQ25, §7.4]; Langlands [38].

items.name: The L-group ᴸH = Ĥ ⋊ Gal(E/F)
items.statement: For H connected reductive over F split over a finite Galois E/F, with dual group (Ĥ, B̂, T̂) over ℤ attached to the dual based root datum and a pinning, Gal(E/F) acts on Ĥ and ᴸH := Ĥ ⋊ Gal(E/F), regarded as a generalised reductive group scheme over O; X^*(T) = X_*(T̂) Gal(E/F)-equivariantly.
items.note: ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.5 plans the pinned split dual group over ℤ and the semidirect L-group.

items.name: Lemma 16.1: the p-power torsion of the connected centre
items.statement: Z(H)^0(F) = (E^× ⊗ M)^{Gal(E/F)} for M the character lattice of Ĥ/Ĥ′; hence μ = (μ_{p^∞}(E) ⊗ M)^{Gal(E/F)} is canonically the p-power torsion Z(H)^0(F)_{p^∞}.
items.note: Borel [9, Prop. 14.2] for X_*(Z(H_E)^0).

items.name: Theorems 16.2–16.4: deformation rings of admissible L-parameters
items.statement: For admissible ρ̄ : Γ_F → ᴸH(k) (composition to Gal(E/F) is γ ↦ γ|_E), the framed ring R^□_ρ̄ is O-flat and a complete intersection of relative dimension dim Ĥ_k([F:ℚ_p] + 1) with R^□/ϖ a complete intersection (Theorem 16.2), reduced with R^□[1/p] normal (Theorem 16.3); if π_1(Ĥ′) is étale and O contains the p^m-th roots of unity (p^m = |Z(H)^0(F)_{p^∞}|), χ ↦ Spec R^{□,χ}_ρ̄ is a canonical bijection between characters of Z(H)^0(F)_{p^∞} and irreducible components, the R^{□,χ} and R^{□,χ}/ϖ being complete-intersection normal domains (Theorem 16.4).
items.note: The canonical label of a component: a Q̄_p-point gives an admissible ψ into ᴸH/Ĥ′, the L-group of Z(H)^0, hence by the local Langlands correspondence for tori (Langlands [38], Birkbeck [4]) a character of Z(H)^0(F), restricted to its p-power torsion.

items.name: The local Langlands correspondence for tori
items.statement: For a torus T over F split by E, continuous admissible parameters Γ_F → ᴸT(Q̄_p) up to T̂-conjugacy (equivalently H¹(Γ_F, T̂(Q̄_p))) correspond to continuous characters T(F) → Q̄_p^× (Langlands [38]; p-adic coefficients: Birkbeck [4]).
items.note: Not planned in the atlas (ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction ES6 treats tori only inside Fargues–Scholze's ℓ ≠ p assignment). Recorded in the Part II's L-group layer as a stated input.

items.name: C-groups and Theorem 16.5
items.statement: The C-group ᶜH (Buzzard–Gee [13, Def. 5.3.2]) sits in 0 → ᴸH → ᶜH →^d 𝔾_m → 0 (109) with ᶜH/Ĥ′ ≅ ᴸH/Ĥ′ × 𝔾_m (110) and ᶜH/Ĥ ≅ Gal(E/F) × 𝔾_m (111). For ρ̄ : Γ_F → ᶜH(k) with d∘ρ̄ ≡ χ_cyc and admissible projection, D^C_ρ̄(A) = {ρ_A lifting ρ̄ with d∘ρ_A = χ_cyc ⊗ A} is pro-represented by R^{□,C}_ρ̄, and Theorems 16.2–16.4 hold for it (Theorem 16.5: M_1 = ℤ, M_2 = X^*(Ĥ/Ĥ′), H_1 = Gal(E/F) × 𝔾_m, H_2 = (Ĥ/Ĥ′) ⋊ Gal(E/F)).
items.note: Motivated by the first two bullet points of Buzzard–Gee [13, Conj. 5.3.4] on Galois representations of C-algebraic automorphic forms.

items.name: Condensed sets
items.statement: A condensed set is an accessible functor ProFin^op → Set sending finite disjoint unions to products and satisfying descent along surjections of profinite sets (equivalently a finite-product-preserving functor on extremally disconnected sets); condensed groups and rings are defined internally; every profinite set, group or ring is one, and every set gives a discrete condensed set.
items.note: Mathlib: CondensedSet (Mathlib/Condensed/Basic.lean), Condensed.discrete, CondensedSet.isDiscrete_tfae.

items.name: Lemmas A.1–A.8: quasi-compact and quasi-separated condensed sets
items.statement: Profinite sets are compact objects (Lemma A.1); surjections of condensed sets are effective epimorphisms (Lemma A.2); X is quasi-compact iff some profinite set surjects onto it (Lemma A.3); quasi-separatedness is tested on pullbacks of the diagonal along profinite sets (Lemma A.4); filtered colimits of qcqs condensed sets along quasi-compact injections are quasi-separated (Lemma A.5); subobjects of quasi-separated condensed sets are quasi-separated (Lemma A.6); a map S → X(*) from a profinite set lifts to at most one map of condensed sets when X is quasi-separated (Lemma A.7); for a closed immersion X ↪ 𝔸ⁿ_R and a quasi-separated condensed R-algebra A, X(A) ↪ Aⁿ is a quasi-compact injection (Lemma A.8).
items.note: Scholze's lectures [52, 53]. VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories VS2 is the atlas's owner of condensed foundations (building on Mathlib's CondensedSet and CondensedMod); these lemmas belong there.
